steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing.

steps.title: Confirm diverter motor first
steps.body: If diverter does not route water between zones, complete §3-13 diverter motor test first.
steps.sourceExcerpt: If diverter does not route water between zones, complete §3-13 diverter motor test first.

steps.title: Position switch harness continuity OK?
steps.body: Power off. Verify diverter position switch and P11 connectors seated. Check harness continuity switch to P11.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power off. Verify diverter position switch and P11 connectors seated. Check harness continuity switch to P11.

steps.title: Continue after Service Diagnostics entry
steps.body: Service Diagnostics cycle should be available (entered via key sequence; cycle starts when door closes). Continue with bench checks below.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Refer to Component Testing; use Service Diagnostics Cycle for live load verification.

steps.title: Position voltage varies 0–8–10 V in Service Diagnostics?
steps.body: Power on. DC volts: red P11-2, black P10-2. Run Service Diagnostics — voltage should pulse 0 V to 8–10 V as diverter reaches each position.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power on. DC volts: red P11-2, black P10-2. Run Service Diagnostics — voltage should pulse 0 V to 8–10 V as diverter reaches each position.

steps.title: Repair harness
steps.body: Repair or replace diverter position switch harness.
steps.oemOutcome: Repair or replace diverter position switch harness.

steps.title: Replace diverter assembly
steps.body: Replace diverter assembly if sensor does not detect positions.
steps.oemOutcome: Replace diverter assembly if sensor does not detect positions.

steps.title: Replace ACU
steps.body: If motor and sensor good but fault persists, replace control.
steps.oemOutcome: If motor and sensor good but fault persists, replace control.
